chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-'Abbas ibn al-'Ala' from Mujahid from his father from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The sins that change the bounties are transgression; the sins that bring regret are murder; and that which brings down curses is injustice; and that which tears the veil is drinking wine; and that which withholds sustenance is adultery; and that which hastens annihilation is severing ties of kinship; and that which repels supplication and darkens the air is disobedience to the parents.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific sins that repel supplication and hasten annihilation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates a precise causal relationship between specific major sins and their distinct spiritual and worldly consequences, reflecting the Shia understanding of divine justice. The narration highlights how transgression (bagh) alters blessings, while disobedience to parents (uquq) not only repels supplication but also darkens the atmosphere, illustrating the tangible impact of sin on the believer's environment. This enumeration serves as a practical guide for self-accountability, linking ethical breaches directly to the erosion of divine favor.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abbas Bin Al A’ala, from Mujahid, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The sins which change the Bounties is the transgression, and the sins which inherit the regret is the murder, and that which brings down the Curses is the injustice, and that which tear apart the Veil is drinking of the wine, and that which withholds the sustenance is the adultery, and that which hastens the annihilation is cutting off of the relationships, and that which repels the supplication and darkens the personal desires is the ingratitude to the parents’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn al-‘Ala’ from Mujahid from his father from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The sins that change the bounties (of Allah) are transgressions, the sins that bring regret are murder, the one that brings hatred is injustice, that which brings disgrace is drinking wine, the sin which holds back the means of living is fornication, the one that hastens one’s perishing is failing to maintain good relations with relatives and the sins that cause the prayers to be rejected and brings darkness (in life) is failing to maintain good relations with parents.”
